question: The sacral hiatus — the entry point for caudal epidural block — is formed by the failure of fusion of which sacral vertebral laminae?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: S1–S2 laminae are typically fused in adults. The hiatus is at the caudal end of the sacrum.
S2–S3 are usually fused. The hiatus results from non-fusion of the most caudal sacral laminae.
Correct. The sacral hiatus is formed by failure of fusion of the S4 and S5 laminae (sometimes S5 alone), leaving a gap covered by the sacrococcygeal membrane — the target for caudal injection.
S3–S4 laminae are generally fused. The hiatus is at the S4–S5 level (or S5 alone), at the caudal apex of the sacrum.

overallFeedback.feedback: The sacral hiatus is located at S4–S5, at the inferior end of the sacrum. Palpate the sacral cornua on either side to identify it before injection.
Correct. S4–S5 non-fusion creates the hiatus. The paired sacral cornua flanking it are the palpable landmarks used to locate it clinically.
